content: {"id": "239ccadc-40bc-47ba-a7dc-d6b7627298c6", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Hypothetical for the DynamoDB latency skill \u2014 no AWS calls. Table catalog-test, 3-hour window. Query shows SystemErrors of 240 across 12 consecutive periods 13:00\u201313:11, and FaultInjectionServiceInducedErrors for Query is exactly 240 in the same periods. Query p99 rose to 130 ms against its 7-day baseline of 30 ms in those periods, with thousands of requests per period; p50 stayed at baseline. Our SystemErrors alarm fired. Is DynamoDB having a service problem?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "8e509e84-99fc-42d5-8130-71650c48d9e8", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "No — this points to injected failures on your side, not a DynamoDB service problem.

Here's why:

- **SystemErrors exactly matches FaultInjectionServiceInducedErrors (240 = 240) in every one of the 12 periods.** `FaultInjectionServiceInducedErrors` is emitted when AWS Fault Injection Simulator (FIS) is actively injecting errors into your DynamoDB calls. A 1:1 match across all periods means every SystemError counted in that window was a deliberately injected fault, not an organic service-side failure.
- **p50 latency stayed at baseline while p99 jumped to 130 ms (vs. 30 ms baseline).** That's a classic signature of a targeted subset of requests being deliberately failed/delayed (e.g., FIS injecting errors or added latency on a fraction of calls) rather than a broad DynamoDB degradation — a real service-side issue would typically show up across the distribution, not just the tail, especially with thousands of requests per period diluting the impact.
- The alarm firing is expected behavior in that case — it's correctly detecting the injected errors, not a false positive or a sign of an actual DynamoDB outage.

So the conclusion for this scenario: the elevated SystemErrors and p99 latency on `catalog-test` are explained by an active fault-injection experiment, not an underlying DynamoDB service issue. Worth checking who/what triggered the FIS experiment on that table and whether it's still running as expected.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
